verses.1: So, what’s the advantage of circumcision? What’s its benefit?
verses.2: In every way, it’s different. First of all, for one thing, people believed in the words of God.
verses.3: Why? If some people do doubt it, does their doubt not destroy their faith in God?
verses.4: May it not happen. Let me, however, be true to God. But every human being is a liar, as it is written: How can you be right in your words, and yet win in the judgment?
verses.5: And if our injustice is equivalent to justice before God, then what should we do? Isn’t it unjust for God to express His wrath in this way? But I’m speaking from a human perspective.
verses.6: May it not happen. For how can God judge the world?
verses.7: But if the truth about God has been distorted in me into a lie, and this lie has become more prominent than the truth itself, then why should I still be judged as a sinner?
verses.8: And we must not act in a way that is disrespectful or offensive. As some people say, “Should we do evil in order to achieve good?” But that kind of behavior deserves punishment.
verses.9: So what? Should we wait? After all, we must consider that both Jews and Greeks are all guilty of sin.
verses.10: As it is written, no one is just.
verses.11: He is not a sinner, he is not someone who seeks out the god.
verses.12: Everyone was dismissed, and they were all called away. It’s not useful to do this; it doesn’t lead to anything. It’s pointless.
verses.13: The tombs of those who were buried there were desecrated; their languages were destroyed. They lay in graves covered with their own lips.
verses.14: Which mouth is filled with bitterness and harshness.
verses.15: Their feet are extremely hot and bloody.
verses.16: difficulties and hardships along their routes.
verses.17: And they did not know what peace really meant.
verses.18: There is no fear of God in their eyes.
verses.19: We know that whatever the law commands those who are subject to it, in order for everyone’s mouth to be sealed and for all people to become guilty before God.
verses.20: For all actions that violate the law will not be justified before him. This is because according to the law, any act of sinning is considered a violation of the law.
verses.21: And now, justice of God is revealed apart from law; it is testified to by both the law and the prophets.
verses.22: But justice of God is given through the faith in Jesus Christ, for all those who believe in Him. Therefore, it isn’t a division at all.
verses.23: For they all were wrong and lost the glory of God.
verses.24: They deserve to receive a gift from Him, through the redemption that comes through Jesus Christ.
verses.25: The God assigned him a “scalable” role, through his own blood, as a sign of His justice. This role involved bearing the sins of those who had committed wrongdoing.
verses.26: In the divine patience, in accordance with the signs of His justice in this present time, so that He may be just and righteous according to Jesus’ teachings.
verses.27: So, what is the basis for this honor? It’s based on law. But by whose law? By the laws of works? No, it’s based on the law of faith.
verses.28: For we consider it to be a right of a person to have credit, regardless of any legal obligations.
verses.29: Is God alone among the Jews? No, he is also among all nations. He is present among all nations.
verses.30: If God is indeed the one who grants forgiveness through faith, and also allows one to be circumcised because of faith.
verses.31: So, will we abolish the law because of our beliefs? No, instead, we will stand by the law.
